facts.raw_span: A 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
altered mental status
febrile and intermittently responsive (Glasgow Coma Scale 10)
left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology was positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage

Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion, and subtle punctate blooming on susceptibility-weighted images
Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
no valvular vegetations
Gram stain was negative
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement

finalists.label: Brain Abscess
finalists.why: The candidate has the most comprehensive evidence from imaging and cerebrospinal fluid analysis, including a hypodense area on CT, T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on MRI, and elevated WBCs in CSF, which together suggest a focal infectious process.
finalists.unexplained: The presence of benzodiazepines and opiates in urine toxicology, which could potentially contribute to altered mental status but does not directly explain the focal neurological findings and imaging results.

finalists.label: Encephalitis
finalists.why: The candidate is supported by evidence of altered mental status, fever, and elevated WBCs in CSF, which are all consistent with an inflammatory process affecting the brain.
finalists.unexplained: The lack of specific findings pointing to a particular cause of encephalitis, such as an identified pathogen or a characteristic imaging pattern.

finalists.label: Toxoplasmosis

Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion, and subtle punctate blooming on susceptibility-weighted images
fails: Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement
Urine toxicology was positive for benzodiazepines and opiates

final.why: The finding of a hypodense area on CT and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on MRI with mass effect and progression on repeat MRI, along with elevated WBCs in CSF, most strongly supports Brain Abscess.
